lines.text: The last four fought on the fifth day. The stands were full before dawn. People paid a crown each to stand on the roofs.
Maric came out burning. He didn't wait for the herald. White fire was already running down his sword before Oswin reached the sand.
Oswin met it with frost, the way he had met Stane. It didn't work. The white fire didn't want air. It didn't want anything. It just ate.
His frost melted off his blade like snow off a roof. Then his cloak caught. Then his breastplate began to glow.
Maric! Stop! Look at your hands, boy! It's eating you!
I'm not your boy! I'm nobody's charity! I'm a Varr!
I felt it before I saw it. Oswin's thread went white hot inside my chest, and then it screamed.
He was down. His sword lay in a puddle of glass. And my brother stood over him with a blade of white fire, raised to finish it.
Maric! No!
He heard me. I will always believe he heard me. He looked up at the royal box, and for one moment he was just my brother.
Then the fire turned around.
It poured out of his eyes and his mouth and the joints of his armour. It wasn't burning outward anymore. It was burning him.
He fell. Nobody caught him. The draught had used him up, and now it was finishing the job.
I don't remember climbing over the rail. Wren says I knocked over the same bishop. Ash cleared a path through the guards without biting anybody.
I held my brother in the sand. He was burning, and I couldn't feel any of it. Not one thread. He had never let me.
Don't... little brother. Don't you dare.
They carried Oswin off on a stretcher. He was still giving Wren advice.
Watch Caddoc's left side. He drops it. Also, I'm fine.
You're on fire.
Slightly.
Lord Maric cannot continue! Sir Oswin cannot continue! The next bout is the final! Wren of Greyhollow, against Brother Caddoc of the Order!
In the royal box, the Grand Measurer wrote something in a small black book, as calmly as a man noting the price of grain.
Tomorrow, Wren would fight for my freedom. Against a man whose rings were bought, and who had never once lost.
The Lord Who Measured Zero. Chapter ninety, coming soon.
